rows.user_input: How many kilograms can I put in the panniers and top box?

output.natural_language: This manual does not give a separate kilogram limit for the panniers or top box. Page 13 says not to exceed the maximum payload defined in the GMA fitting instructions for panniers and top boxes, and those instructions are not in this manual. The manual's overall maximum payload is 196 kg, including rider, pillion and accessories, so the luggage allowance is what remains after rider and pillion weight are subtracted (page 115). Gross vehicle weight is 394 kg (page 18). Warnings: do not load weight or install accessories incorrectly, as this can affect stability and handling and could cause a serious accident (page 13). Do not exceed 110 km/h when riding solo, with a pillion, or with payload on an accessory-equipped motorcycle (page 12). Keep luggage weight close to the motorcycle and as low as possible, distribute it evenly on both sides, and do not load bulky items behind the rider or add weight to the handlebars or front forks (pages 12-13). Re-check luggage periodically so it stays secure (page 13). For the exact pannier and top box limit, contact Royal Enfield support.

The adjuster is a 6-step adjuster, and the manual says it is kept at the first notch by default (PDF page 116). The setting table on PDF page 117 is garbled in the source conversion, so I can't reliably match a notch to the rider-only row. The manual also says the best preload is set for the rider's weight plus any luggage and passenger. Before adjusting, rest the motorcycle on the center stand, make sure tyre pressure is at the recommended 32 psi front and rear (PDF page 117), and clean the adjuster of dirt and debris. Adjusting requires the C-spanner from the tool kit, and an extension tube may be used for leverage (PDF page 116). Because the solo notch can't be confirmed from the manual, please check with Royal Enfield Support or an Authorised Dealer before changing the setting.

rows.user_input: The engine does not start.

output.natural_language: The manual's first check for an engine that does not start is the ignition and kill switch. Turn the ignition key to ON and set the engine kill switch on the right handlebar to RUN. Do not hold the starter button for more than 5 seconds. If the engine does not start within 5 seconds, release the starter, wait about 5 seconds, then try again. After three successive cranking attempts, wait 15 to 20 seconds before cranking again. Repeated long cranking can drain the battery below 10 V. If the engine still will not start, check fuel level and fuses as the manual describes, and contact an Authorised Royal Enfield Service Centre if the problem persists.

rows.user_input: How many kilograms can I put in the panniers and top box?

output.natural_language: The manual does not give a separate kg limit for panniers or the top box. It says not to exceed the maximum payload defined in the GMA (Genuine Motorcycle Accessories) fitting instructions for those accessories, so check those instructions for your specific pannier and top box. The manual's overall payload figure is up to 196 kg, including rider weight, pillion weight and accessories. Gross vehicle weight is 394 kg, and kerb weight (90% fuel and oil) is 196 kg. Do not load weight or install accessories incorrectly, because this can affect stability and handling and could cause an accident. Keep luggage weight low and close to the motorcycle, distribute it evenly on both sides, and do not load bulky items behind the rider. Do not exceed 110 km/h when riding solo, with a pillion, or with payload on an accessory-equipped motorcycle. Re-check that luggage is secured periodically, since loose luggage can shift while riding.

The preload setting should match rider weight plus any luggage and passenger (PDF page 116). Max payload is 196 kg including rider, pillion, and accessories (PDF page 117). rows.user_input: The engine does not start.

output.natural_language: Engine not starting is covered in the troubleshooting table. First check the ignition is ON and the engine kill switch is set to RUN, then check fuel level. Starting sequence: put the bike in neutral (move it gently back and forth while shifting if needed), pull the clutch lever fully in, then press and hold the electric start switch for no more than 5 seconds. If the engine does not start, release it and wait about 5 seconds before retrying. After three successive cranking attempts, wait 15 to 20 seconds. Do not hold the starter for long periods, as this can drain the battery below 10 V. If the engine still does not start, or the battery is weak or discharged, take the motorcycle to a Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre. WARNING: Keep the side stand fully retracted before riding. Do not press the starter more than 5 seconds at a time.
